passages.note: Clere is in the Nay list on House 3rd reading of the state RFRA; a No vote rejects the exemption statute but matches no clause of any rung on the other side.
passages.actor_quote: Brown, C Hale Niezgodski Stemler Clere Kersey Pelath Summers

passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled text of the bill Clere voted against: a general strict-scrutiny exemption statute, which the annex places at rung 4.
Bill-details page for the same instrument; it shows the bill is single-subject and lists authors and sponsors, among whom Clere does not appear, so it prints no act of his and no operative text.

rows.reasoning: Clere voted Nay on SB 101 (2015), whose operative section lets a governmental entity burden religious exercise only where that burden "is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest" — the general exemption statute that matches "protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions from laws that conflict with sincere religious beliefs." Voting it down rejects that rung, but it matches no clause of "prohibit religious exemptions from civil rights and anti-discrimination laws.", of "protect religious freedom while ensuring it doesn't override anti-discrimination protections in employment and housing.", or of "balance protecting religious practices with maintaining equal treatment under the law for all citizens." Ruling out the other rungs is not evidence for the one left (V4.2), so the record shows only the side.
